## Masked Matter-Horn

The goggle-wearing, freeze-ray-firing leader of the Power Ponies, defenders of comic-book Maretropolis. In *Friendship Is Magic*, **Twilight Sparkle temporarily becomes Masked Matter-Horn** when Spike's enchanted comic pulls the group inside. The comic's **original heroine is a distinct character**, whose civilian identity, **Trot Summers**, is given in licensed merchandise—not another name for Twilight.

- **Appearance and powers:** Twilight's version has a violet coat and wings, a dark mane with a pink stripe, a burgundy suit, pale-blue chest armor, gold-rimmed goggles, and star-marked boots; her horn shoots freezing and other energy beams. The original comic Matter-Horn is a **unicorn**, with a different mane and **mountain emblems** in place of Twilight's stars. [Character and design history](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Power_Ponies_%28characters%29).
- **Name and identity:** Spike calls her “Masked Matter-Horn” in *Power Ponies* (2013); the name plays on the Matterhorn mountain and a unicorn's horn. Enterplay's licensed **Power Ponies card PP1** supplies **Trot Summers** and her Professor Celestia's School for Gifted Youth backstory—merchandise lore, **not dialogue or a reveal in the TV episode**. [Trading-card catalog](https://data.mlpmerch.com/tc/type/power-ponies/).
- **Speaking:** **Yes** as Twilight in *Power Ponies* (S4E6), voiced by **Tara Strong**. The separate original heroine speaks in the IDW comic but has **no separately verified animated voice credit**. [Episode cast](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3098722/fullcredits/).
- **Appearances:** *Friendship Is Magic*, **S4E6 “Power Ponies”** (December 21, 2013); the original Power Ponies in **IDW's *My Little Pony Annual 2014***; and a costume/film-set nod in *Equestria Girls: Movie Magic*, where **human Sci-Twi is mistaken for the actress playing Matter-Horn**—not the comic heroine herself. Later episodes reference Spike's comics. [Movie Magic context](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Twilight_Sparkle_%28Sci-Twi%29).

## Important moments

1. **Mastering the freeze ray** — *“Power Ponies,” S4E6.* After her initial powers fizzle, Twilight successfully fires a freeze ray while fighting the Mane-iac's henchponies. [Official full episode](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wNG7jmYu-NY) — **scene timestamp unavailable**.
2. **Standing up for Hum Drum** — *“Power Ponies,” S4E6.* When Mane-iac calls the supposedly powerless Spike useless, Twilight insists he always comes through when needed; his ensuing rescue vindicates her faith. [Episode transcript](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/Power_Ponies) — **scene timestamp unavailable**.
3. **The teamwork boast unravels** — *IDW, “Power Ponies,” *My Little Pony Annual 2014* (comic; no season/episode number).* Trot publicly credits teamwork for their success, but the team privately bickers and later loses its powers to united villains. [Comic plot and credits](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/My_Little_Pony_Annual_2014) — **video timestamp not applicable**.
4. **Learning from the sidekick** — *IDW, “Power Ponies,” *My Little Pony Annual 2014*.* Hum Drum teaches her fractured team the value of friendship, enabling it to cooperate and beat the villains; the leader must accept help to lead well. [Publisher and creative-team details](https://data.mlpmerch.com/comic-covers/issue/annual/2/) — **video timestamp not applicable**.
